The body's deadlock chain was verified against the code (not taken on faith):

1. **The husk wait DOES sit inside the flock.** `scripts/task.py` `main()` (L2202-2219)
   dispatches straight to the subcommand without resolving the repo root first; every
   mutation body starts `with _locked(): ... find_task_path(N)` (e.g. `set_body`, L5913),
   and `find_task_path` (L4896) → `_load_registry` → `registry_path()` → `tasks_dir()` →
   `repo_root()`. The lazy `lru_cache` resolver therefore first runs — and pays the
   bounded husk wait (L440-549, default 120 s) — while the writer already holds
   `~/.task-workflow/lock`. The flock itself (L797-810) is a plain blocking `LOCK_EX`
   with no timeout, so ~15 concurrent writers starve every other writer.
2. **The helper's only lock acquisition is the one that starves.**
   `sync_repo_root.acquire_task_workflow_lock` (L724-748) has exactly ONE caller —
   `_run_locked` L1952 — and it gates `preflight()` (L765-892), which is where the
   sanctioned husk clearing lives. Bound `EPM_ROOT_SYNC_LOCK2_WAIT_S` default 120 s,
   matching the observed `state=error exit=5`.
3. **The encoded false assumption is a comment.** `task_workflow.py` L500-503 asserts
   "No deadlock while a caller waits here holding the task-workflow flock ... the
   observed rebase never needs the flock to finish." True for a LIVE rebase that the
   helper itself drives; FALSE for an ABANDONED husk, where nobody will ever finish it
   and the only sanctioned clearer needs the very flock the waiters hold.
4. **Husk-age thresholds** (`sync_repo_root` L251-270): stale at
   `EPM_ROOT_SYNC_HUSK_AGE_S` = 3600 s; the young-husk liveness downgrade window is
   `EPM_ROOT_SYNC_HUSK_MIN_AGE_S` = 600 s .. 3600 s, gated on
   `_probe_git_liveness` returning `none`.
5. **Second-order finding for the plan (new, not in the body):** the liveness probe
   (L652-721) attributes any `comm == "git"` process by its cwd. Each waiting writer
   re-probes with a `symbolic-ref` subprocess every 2 s, and fleet sessions run with cwd
   at the repo root, so those short-lived read-only probes can be attributed as a live
   "holder" — the young-husk downgrade can be defeated by the waiters' own polling, in
   exactly the scenario it exists for. Consequence: convergence for a 600-3600 s husk
   may have to wait for the stale threshold. To evaluate at plan time; the ordering fix
   is independent of it.
6. **Autostash surfaces** (all read-only today): `_autostash_entries` (L1287),
   `_triage_autostash` (L1651), `_warn_autostash_backlog` (L895), `_stash_file_list`

   (`autonomous_session_watch.py` L9112) fires one repo-level Telegram push keyed on a
   set fingerprint, posts NO task markers, and names human companion task #1736 — i.e.
   the alert has no owner, which is the non-convergence the body reports.
